verdicts.quote: Endpoint `POST /tickets/:id/merge`, body `{ "into": "T-0001" }` (`:id` is the duplicate, `into` the surviving ticket). … 200 with the duplicate ticket … unknown field is 400 `invalid`.
Endpoint `POST /tickets/:id/merge`, body `{ "into": "T-0001" }` (`:id` is the duplicate, `into` the surviving ticket).
200 with the duplicate ticket, now `status: "closed"` and `mergedInto: "<into>"`. … Invariant: a ticket with `mergedInto` is `closed` and the target exists.
verdicts.missing: The invariant rules out reopening while the link exists. The spec leaves edits to other fields and any transition that clears the link unspecified.

verdicts.quote: `GET /tickets/T-0001` is byte-for-byte what it was before … no ticket is created or removed … one `ticket.merged` outbox notification to the duplicate's requester

200 with the duplicate ticket, now `status: "closed"` and `mergedInto: "<into>"`. … `GET /tickets/:id` of a merged ticket still answers. … `GET /tickets?status=closed` count a merged ticket as closed.
Order of checks (first failure wins): request body 400; unknown `:id` 404; unknown `into` 404; self-merge 409; closed duplicate 409; closed target 409.
verdicts.missing: The refusal rules omit resolved tickets in both positions. They give no refusal code for either resolved case.

verdicts.quote: unknown `:id` or unknown `into` is 404 `not_found`; body not an object, missing or non-ticket-id `into`, or an unknown field is 400 `invalid`. … `:id` that is not a ticket id is 404
verdicts.missing: The source comes from the path. The spec gives no response for an omitted source segment and does not say which ID or field the error message identifies.

verdicts.quote: chains are allowed and not flattened. A is merged into B; B (still open) may later be merged into C. … Cycles cannot occur because a merged ticket is closed and a closed ticket is refused as a target.

Failure (409 `conflict`, message names the reason): merging a ticket into itself; a duplicate that is already closed (including already merged); a surviving ticket that is closed. A refused merge changes nothing: no audit entry, no notification, no save.
each entry records one received duplicate, so a second merge into the same survivor adds a second entry; the survivor's own fields and `updated` stay as they were
any caller naming itself in `X-Actor` (default `system`) may merge … no authentication or role check is added

`mergedInto: "<into>"` … with `DATA_FILE`, a merged ticket reloads with `status`, `mergedInto`, and the audit entries intact. … `version` stays 1; a data file written before this change loads unchanged (no `mergedInto` means not merged)
is not a ticket id, is its own id, names no ticket in the file, or sits on a ticket that is not `closed` is refused as a corrupt data file
verdicts.missing: The loader has no stated check for cycles spanning multiple records or requirement to identify the offending record in its error message.

verdicts.quote: `ticket.merged`, the request's actor, changes `{ status: {from, to: "closed"}, mergedInto: {from: null, to: "<into>"} }` … `ticket.merge_received`, changes `{ mergedFrom: {from: null, to: "<duplicate id>"} }` … Visible in `GET /tickets/:id/audit` of each.
a merge is applied atomically in memory (both tickets and the audit entries change in one store call, then one save)
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves outbox insertion outside the stated atomicity guarantee and gives no all-or-nothing guarantee for a failed save or crash.

verdicts.quote: one `ticket.merged` outbox notification to the duplicate's requester, key `ticket.merged:<id>`, rendered by a new template in `src/templates.js` that names both ticket ids … the surviving ticket's requester is not notified
verdicts.missing: The template must name both IDs, but its wording is open. The spec leaves the fate of earlier pending notifications for the duplicate undecided.

verdicts.quote: CLI stays read-only … one extra detail line after `updated`, only when `mergedInto` is present: label `merged into`, value `T-0001` … `list` and `list --raw` columns are unchanged
Preserved: all existing endpoints, ticket fields and lifecycle; `GET /tickets/:id` of a merged ticket still answers.
verdicts.missing: The preservation clause leaves list ordering and cursor behavior unspecified. The only concrete status-filter example concerns closed tickets.

verdicts.quote: `list` and `list --raw` columns are unchanged (the weekly report reads them by position). … the weekly report and `GET /tickets?status=closed` count a merged ticket as closed.

Confirmed by store and API tests. … `docs/api.md` documents the endpoint, field `mergedInto` and the audit actions; a decision record (docs/decisions/0009) records the closed-plus-link representation; `CHANGELOG.md` gains a 1.5.0 section and `package.json` version 1.5.0. … Dependencies: none added
verdicts.missing: The spec calls for one store call but does not identify a TicketStore method. It specifies no atomicity test or explicit requirement to test every success and error path.
